newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat harvest advances in warm, dry weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat harvest advances in warm, dry weather.

text.p: Harvesting of Texas wheat progressed during the week ended Sunday amid warm, dry weather, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
The warmer temperatures also aided growth and maturing of crops, the report said.
Wheat was 42 percent harvested, against 26 last week, 74 last year and 56 percent on average.
The condition of the state's wheat crop was rated 8 percent excellent, 42 good, 36 fair, 12 poor and 2 percent very poor.
Corn was 38 percent silked, against 55 percent last year and 54 on average. Corn condition improved and was rated 33 percent excellent, 51 good, 12 fair, three poor and one percent very poor.
Sorghum was 32 percent headed versus 49 a year ago and 52 percent on average. Sorghum was rated 25 percent excellent, 53 good, 18 fair, three good and one excellent.
Sunflowers were 61 percent planted versus 72 a year ago and 74 on average. Cotton was 28 percent squaring, versus 31 last year and 27 on average.
